title: Wall Street Cuts Nvidia Price Targets By 25% Despite Latest Reversal
detail:
Wall Street Cuts Nvidia Price Targets By 25% Despite Latest Reversal
Lockridge Okoth
Tue, November 24, 2026 at 3:12 PM EST 2 min read
NVDA
BAC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Several Wall Street firms and analysts have revised their Nvidia price targets this week. Oppenheimer cut its target to $250 from $315. Bank of America now sits at $280, down from $350 in August.

The cuts came a day after Nvidia reinstated CEO Jensen Huang following a scandal. The average target of $233.36 still sits 54% above Tuesday's price near $151.

Nvidia (NVDA) Stock Forecast & Price Target. Source: TipRanks
Wall Street's New Nvidia Price Outlook

An upgrade lifts a firm's rating, such as from Hold to Buy. A price target is the firm's estimate of where the stock will trade in 12 months. This week, some firms raised one and lowered the other.

Oppenheimer's upgrade came with a $65 cut to its target

Phillip Securities kept its Buy rating but lowered its target by 25%, to $225 from $300.

Bank of America kept its Buy rating. Its $350 August target has been reduced to $280.

Even the consensus sits below Nvidia's old high. The $233.36 average is under the $243.37 peak the stock reached before the scandal broke on Nov. 8.

Not every firm cut. Citi raised its target to $240 from $225, and Melius Research upgraded at $220, up from $185.

StoneX upgraded to Buy at $270, while Raymond James kept the Street's highest target at $350.

Nvidia Price Targets Before and After Huang's Return. Source: BeInCrypto, data from TipRanks

The upgrades followed the board's vote to reinstate Huang as CEO. The bulls' case rests on earnings.

Nvidia raised its fiscal 2028 guidance and expects 75% revenue growth that year, Motley Fool reported.

Even after Monday's 31.5% jump, the stock traded near 10 times next year's expected earnings.

There are Still Unresolved Problems at Nvidia

Matt Maley, chief market strategist at Miller Tabak + Co., told Bloomberg the rebound may only have bought the AI trade time.

He pointed to delayed data-center construction, price-sensitive customers and growing scrutiny.

Maley also flagged Nvidia's circular financing, where the company funds customers that then buy its chips. Bloomberg reported that he called the sector a house of cards.

The SEC is investigating whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors. US officials are also investigating Megaspeed, a Singapore firm accused of diverting Nvidia chips to China.

Huang faces a closed-door interview with three House committees on Dec. 1.

Meanwhile, Goldman Sachs reiterated Buy at $220, but its trading desk said the rebound had not settled the chip sector's problems.

The selling spread across chipmakers on Tuesday, a day after supplier TSMC jumped 16% on the Nvidia news. AMD fell nearly 12%, and the Nasdaq dropped 2.45%.

title: Quants Unwind Bond Shorts as Stock Swoon Drives Traders to Safety

Quants Unwind Bond Shorts as Stock Swoon Drives Traders to Safety

Trade BAC on Coinbase

(Bloomberg) -- Trend-chasing quant funds are trimming their long-held short positions in US Treasuries, fueling a bond rally as an equity selloff revives haven demand for government debt.

Most Read from Bloomberg

Nvidia Rehires Huang in Stunning Reversal After Trump Push

China Sentences Official to Death for Spying for Foreign Power

Nvidia Board Reinstated CEO Without Consulting Management

Nasdaq 100 Sinks as AI Rout Fuels Gains in Bonds: Markets Wrap

Stocks Jump Most Since April 2025 as Huang Is Back: Markets Wrap

Commodity trading advisers — which seek to profit from momentum across asset classes — have reduced their Treasury shorts to about half their September peak, a Bank of America Corp. model shows. The $5 billion iMGP DBi Managed Futures Strategy exchange-traded fund, which aims to replicate trend-following strategies, cut its short duration exposure — a measure of interest-rate risk — to about negative 6.4 years as of Monday, from negative 7.1 years a week earlier.

CTAs, an investment cohort estimated to manage more than $400 billion, have been consistently betting against Treasuries this year as an oil-price spike, elevated inflation and the artificial-intelligence boom pushed 10-year yields to about 5.36% in October — the highest in more than two decades.

Since then, a swift unwind of the AI trade in stocks has clouded the growth outlook, pushing the 10-year yield down to about 4.9% and prompting trend followers to reduce short wagers. The group is still pessimistic overall with the Federal Reserve expected to raise interest rates again as soon as next month.

While the bearish trend in bonds remains intact, "it's a little bit choppier now than it was earlier this year," said Andrew Beer, founder of Dynamic Beta Investments, which manages the iMGP ETF.

The fund returned more than 17% this year through October, with much of the gain coming from long oil positions. Short Treasuries wagers were profitable until October, when the bond rally cost the position more than 3 percentage points and reduced its contribution to this year's return to about 1 percentage point. The ETF is now up about 14% this year through Monday.

Despite the setback, Beer said CTAs still have a "meaningful" bet on rising interest rates, reflecting concerns about sticky inflation and persistent fiscal deficits.

But it may not take much for the remaining bearish positions to unravel. Bank of America's model shows a roughly 20- to 25-basis-point drop in yields across the curve "would likely unwind most of the remaining shorts," said Chintan Kotecha, a derivatives analyst at the bank.

Berkshire Hathaway's (NYSE:BRKA) (NYSE:BRKB) latest 13F filing was released last week, and, as in prior quarters, the "House that Warren Buffett Built" continues to pare down its position in Bank of America (NYSE:BAC). During the quarter ended Sept. 30, Berkshire sold 27.5 million shares, reducing its stake by 5.7%.

Following this sale, Berkshire now owns just 455.9 million shares, down from a peak of over 1 billion during mid-2024. Yet while the holding company continues to reduce this position, the motivation remains unclear.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Warren Buffett. Image source: The Motley Fool.

Berkshire's likely reason for selling BofA ranges widely

Berkshire Hathaway's sale of its Bank of America position began two years ago, when Warren Buffett was still at the helm, and has continued since Greg Abel became CEO last January. Berkshire and its leadership have not made any explicit statements about this investment decision, leaving a wide range of possible reasons for the continued selling.

On one hand, Berkshire may be concerned about interest rate trends and sees a strong chance that shares, already pulling back in recent months from the mid-$60s to the high-$40s per share, will continue to slide lower. On the other hand, Berkshire first built up its Bank of America stake well over a decade ago. In Buffett and Abel's view, it is time to take profits and reinvest in new opportunities.

Should you buy, sell, or hold Bank of America stock?

As with other bank stocks, Bank of America has come under pressure amid concerns about rate hikes. So far, however, BofA has continued to deliver strong results, as seen in its recent Q3 2026 earnings release. The stock trades for just 9 times forward earnings, and at only a 20% premium to book value.

It also has a forward yield of 2.7%, a more-than-decade-long track record of consecutive annual dividend increases, and dividend growth has averaged in the high single digits in recent years. Although interest rate news still warrants caution, I wouldn't automatically put this stock in the "avoid" pile just because Berkshire is selling.

title: Is Bank of America's Attractive Valuation Enough to Buy the Stock?
detail:
Is Bank of America's Attractive Valuation Enough to Buy the Stock?
Nikita Kataruka
Tue, November 24, 2026 at 10:16 AM EST 6 min read
BAC
JPM
MS
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Bank of America BAC appears relatively inexpensive compared with the industry and major banking peers, as reflected in its forward 12-month price-to-sales (P/S) ratio. The metric, which compares a company's stock price with its revenues, is widely used to assess valuation, as sales are generally less susceptible to accounting adjustments than earnings.

Bank of America currently trades at a forward 12-month P/S multiple of 2.55X, considerably below the industry average of 3.90X. BAC's valuation also remains below the upper end of its five-year historical range, suggesting potential room for multiple expansion if investor sentiment improves.

P/S (F12M)
Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The discount becomes more evident when compared with industry peers. JPMorgan JPM and Morgan Stanley MS trade at forward 12-month P/S multiples of 3.89X and 3.14X, respectively.

BAC's lower multiple indicates that the market is valuing its revenue base more conservatively than those of the peers, despite the extensive banking operations and established market presence.

This valuation disparity could provide scope for upside if Bank of America delivers sustained earnings growth and stronger operating performance, prompting investors to assign a higher multiple to its shares. However, a lower valuation does not necessarily indicate an attractive investment opportunity, as differences in profitability, growth expectations and risk profiles can justify varying multiples. Therefore, BAC's discounted valuation should be assessed alongside its underlying fundamentals and growth prospects.

Key Factors Supporting Bank of America

Robust Top-Line Growth: Bank of America has been witnessing an increase in revenues over the past several years. Total net revenues witnessed a compound annual growth rate ("CAGR") of 5.7% over the last five years (2020-2025), with the uptrend continuing in the first nine months of 2026.

Revenue Trend
Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The rise has been driven by consistent loan growth (net loans and leases saw a CAGR of 5.2% over the same time frame) and a favorable interest rate backdrop, along with a decent rise in fee income (total non-interest income witnessed a CAGR of 4.7%).

Despite declines in interest rates in 2024 and 2025, the company's net interest income ("NII") saw a CAGR of 6.7% in the five years ended 2025, primarily supported by increasing loan balances. The uptrend for NII continued in the first nine months of 2026.

Supported by resilient loan and deposit growth, favorable fixed-rate asset repricing and disciplined balance sheet management, BAC's NII is expected to continue to improve in the near term. This, coupled with fee income growth, will likely keep supporting revenue expansion.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for BAC's 2026 and 2027 revenues is pegged at $122.7 billion and $131 billion, which indicates year-over-year growth rates of 11.3% and 6.8%, respectively.

Key Takeaways

Bank of America reiterated its Buy rating and $100 price target on Wells Fargo, 25% above its Nov. 23 close.

At $100, Wells Fargo would trade at about 2.2x tangible book value. That's above its five-year high and closer to what banks with returns like JPMorgan's command.

Wells Fargo's return on tangible common equity rose to 16.3% in the third quarter, but its tangible book value per share has barely grown in a year.

The returns case looks real, but $100 depends on book value growth and spare capital that Wells Fargo doesn't have yet. Mid-January's results are the next test.

Wells Fargo (WFC:NYSE) closed at $80.00 on Nov. 23, 17% below its January closing high of $96.39. Bank of America (BAC:NYSE) analyst Ebrahim Poonawala sees it topping that high. Last week, he reiterated his Buy rating and $100 price target, 25% above that close, though still below the $107 he set in January.

That would price Wells Fargo at a multiple of tangible book value it hasn't reached in five years. Multiples like that usually go to banks earning what JPMorgan Chase (JPM:NYSE) earns: a 20% return on tangible common equity in the third quarter.

The bench is filling up

Poonawala's case rests on the leadership Wells Fargo is building and a business growing in more places at once. Third-quarter results on Oct. 13 showed the second part: EPS rose 13% to $1.87, and average loans and deposits each grew 11%. Return on tangible common equity (ROTCE) reached 16.3%, against a 17% to 18% target, and CEO Charlie Scharf said on the call that "ultimately, our targets should be higher." On leadership, Bloomberg reported on Nov. 18 that Wells Fargo plans to make JPMorgan executive Allison Beer its next chief operating officer.

title: Nvidia Added $954 Billion In A Day. Is Jensen Huang Too Big To Fire?
detail:
Nvidia Added $954 Billion In A Day. Is Jensen Huang Too Big To Fire?
Trefis Team
Tue, November 24, 2026 at 6:39 AM EST 8 min read
NVDA
AAPL
BAC
C
WFC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

After the 2008 financial crisis, Washington decided that some banks were too big to fail. Between Nov 12 and Nov 23, the White House showed it holds the same view about at least one person. He is Jensen Huang, the co-founder and chief executive of Nvidia.

On Nov 12, Nvidia announced that Huang had resigned as chief executive. The board later said the reason was personal behavior at odds with its code of conduct. His exit came weeks after reports that US intelligence suspected a woman close to him of working for China. She is a former executive of a Singapore cloud computing firm. That day, the President suggested Apple's Tim Cook take over. On Nov 17, the board's new chair said it did not intend to bring Huang back.

On Friday, Nov 20, President Trump said he would like to see Huang "make a big apology and go back." On Monday, Nov 23, Nvidia announced that the board had reinstated him. Its filing said this came after "input from senior levels of the United States government." "I made the deal," the President told CNBC.

Investors cheered. Nvidia's stock rose 31.5% on Monday to $165.05, its biggest one-day gain since May 2003. It added about $954 billion of market value in a single session. Some of that was a rebound. Nvidia had fallen 14% on Friday, the day Reuters reported that SEC staff were examining potential accounting issues there. The S&P 500 fund (SPY) also rose 4.7% on Monday. Even beyond the market's move, Nvidia gained about $810 billion that day. Measured from Thursday's close, before Friday's report, the gain beyond the market was about $430 billion.

Nvidia swung from a 14% fall on Friday to a 31.5% gain on Monday. If you are waiting for a calmer moment to buy, your cash can earn something while you wait. The return, by the numbers: Monday, Nov 23

1

2

3

4

Source: Trefis, closes on Nov 19, Nov 20 and Nov 23. Market values are from shares outstanding, and bank values are at the Nov 23 close. The gain beyond the market is Nvidia's return minus the S&P 500 fund's, times Nvidia's value at the start. The start is Nov 20 for the day and Nov 19 for the two days.

What Did Washington Do About The Banks?

The trouble began in 2007, when mortgage losses started to surface. It peaked in September 2008, when Lehman Brothers failed and the government rescued AIG. The new rules came after. The first bank stress tests came in 2009. Then the Dodd-Frank Act of 2010 created a council of regulators. It could label firms "systemically important" and hold them to stricter rules. From their 2007 highs to the March 2009 lows, Citigroup's stock fell 98% and AIG's 99.5%. The S&P 500 fund lost 55%.

Why banks? Because they are the pipe for money. When the Fed cuts rates or pumps in cash, it works through banks. Banks carry the money to everyone else. If the pipe breaks, the whole economy suffers. So the pipe gets regulated.

What Are The Three Tests?

In 2012, regulators wrote down how they would judge which firms are systemically important. They listed six questions. Three matter here. How big is the firm? How connected is it? Could anyone else step in quickly and do what it does? They called the last one substitutability. The first two measure the company. The third measures the man.

Nvidia is big. It was worth about $4 trillion at Monday's close, roughly 6.4% of the S&P 500. It is also connected. Nvidia has become the pipe for artificial intelligence. Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle spent $691 billion on capital spending over the past year. Much of it went into data centers built around Nvidia's chips. When Huang came back, its suppliers and customers rose with it.

What about the third test? Could anyone else do Huang's job? Investors answered louder on his return than on his exit. Nvidia fell 4.3% the day his resignation was announced. It rose 31.5% the day he came back. Even measured from before Friday's SEC report, the gain beyond the market was about $430 billion. That is more than Bank of America is worth. In our view, it was a verdict on what Nvidia is without him. We asked that question on Nov 12 in What Happens To Nvidia Stock Without Jensen Huang?

Here the bank comparison stops working. After 2008, the fix for a bank too big to fail was to make it less special. Banks had to hold more capital to absorb losses. They also needed a "living will," a plan for winding the bank down without a bailout. The point was to make any one bank replaceable. None of that works for a founder. The only living will for a person is a successor ready on day one. Nvidia has not named one in public.

Who Decides When He Goes?

The other change is who decides, and how fast. Steve Jobs needed 12 years to get back into Apple. Huang needed 11 days.

Jensen Huang, Nvidia

Source: Trefis. Time from the announced exit to the announced return, in days or years.

A comeback is often a board's call. Bob Iger's return to Disney in 2022 was one. In these three, the decision moved further from the boardroom. First it was the board, then the staff and the biggest investor, and now the White House. Huang also differs from Mark Zuckerberg or Google's founders. He owns only a small slice of Nvidia and holds no special voting shares. He was not protected by control. He was protected by the market and by the President.

So, Is This An Era Of Systemically Important Individuals?

Yes, in practice, though not in law. No council has designated Huang, and no rule names him. But investors priced his return like a rescue. And the government treated his job as a matter of national interest. In his case that was literal. The reports around his exit raised a national-security question. The board brought him back only after saying it was confident his reinstatement "poses no national security risk."

A ready successor lowers the cost of losing one leader. When Steve Jobs stepped down in 2011, Tim Cook was in place. Apple's stock slipped 0.65%. A year later it was up 77%, against 22% for the S&P 500 fund. Nvidia had no named successor. The fear of losing one leader is old. A government acting on that fear is new.

This series takes up three more questions. Has America depended on one person before? What can Washington actually do about it? And is Elon Musk one, too? Part 2 of 4 is America Has Had Indispensable Men Before. Why Is Jensen Huang Different?

What Does It Mean For Your Money?

Key-person risk is the risk that a company depends on one person. It used to be a paragraph in a company's annual report. Now it is in your index fund. At Monday's close, Nvidia, Meta and Tesla, all run by their founders, were worth $7.0 trillion. That is about 10% of the S&P 500's value. Then add Alphabet and Oracle, whose founders hold the most votes. Add Amazon too, which Jeff Bezos chairs. The total is $13.6 trillion, about 19%. So roughly one dollar in five of a plain index fund rides, in part, on a handful of founders.

Two things are worth watching. Will Nvidia name an emergency successor, its own living will? And will other boards start checking with Washington before they act? Congress also plans hearings in early December.

That one dollar in five is easy to miss. When so much rides on one company and one person, it helps to spread your money across many strong companies. Then no single exit decides how you do.

BofA says Associated Banc-Corp's commercial and industrial loan growth has not structurally stalled, but share gains are needed to offset Midwest softness, citing flat Chicago Fed district activity and tariff damage to the region. It does not blame weaker third-quarter growth on gaps between hiring cohorts; management flagged the slowdown in July, and commercial and business loans would have risen 2% sequentially excluding a $210mn-plus mortgage warehouse decline. Commerce Bancshares

BofA says Commerce Bancshares can re-rate without a credit cycle only narrowly, requiring better revenue growth, improved operating leverage and faster capital deployment. The shares trade at a 6% premium to high-quality peers, versus 39% in 2024, and a 17% premium to the KBW Regional Banking Index on 2027 earnings. Slower loan growth expectations and downward pre-provision net revenue revisions cap the multiple. The buyback is the clearest near-term lever, with BofA expecting faster repurchases in the fourth quarter as shares trade 9% below the third-quarter average purchase price. It rates CBSH Neutral with a $68 price objective.

In a research report, the bank said consumer staples had attracted renewed investor interest after the U.S. midterm elections, partly as an alternative to the artificial intelligence trade.

BofA also sees a potential fundamental case for the sector, with affordability initiatives and possible improvements in consumer sentiment supporting demand, although it cautioned that no new policy measures had yet been announced.

Keurig Dr Pepper Inc

BofA sees Keurig Dr Pepper as one of the most likely beneficiaries if investors reduce their exposure to Coca-Cola.

The company remains relevant to institutional investors ahead of its planned separation of its beverage and coffee operations. BofA has a "buy" rating and a $40 price target, pointing to potential synergies, wider adoption of Keurig brewers and pods, and scope for reduced volatility in its coffee business.

Procter & Gamble Company

The brokerage also identifies P&G as a potential beneficiary of a rotation away from Coca-Cola. It sees improving North American sales momentum, supported by pricing and productivity initiatives, while lower oil prices towards $70 a barrel could provide additional upside. BofA maintains a "buy" rating and a $185 price target.

Coca-Cola Company

Despite valuation concerns, BofA remains positive on Coca-Cola for 2027, expecting its approximately 5% underlying revenue growth trajectory to continue despite challenging comparisons.

Pricing support from bottler inflation, a stronger product mix from Fairlife and Topo Chico, and refranchising opportunities could help lift operating margins into the high-30% range. The bank has a "buy" rating and a $100 target.

Mondelez International

BofA considers Mondelez relatively well positioned for 2027, citing its earnings visibility, emerging-market exposure and strong position in snacking categories that have shown resilience during inflation. Its $73 price target accompanies a "buy" rating.

Colgate-Palmolive Company

The brokerage sees scope for further market-share gains in the U.S. and emerging markets, alongside margin expansion as commodity-cost pressures ease. BofA has a "buy" rating and a $105 price target.

Monster Beverage Corporation

BofA highlighted Monster as a potential long idea, particularly for European investors. It believes concerns about a slowdown in U.S. product innovation are overstated, noting that international markets continue to grow by more than 20%. The bank has a "buy" rating and a $54 price target.

Primo Brands Corporation

BofA sees Primo Brands as a potential beneficiary if geopolitical conflicts ease, with improving sales trends and cost synergies providing possible earnings support. It has a "buy" rating and a $29 price target.

Vita Coco Company

The brokerage also identifies Vita Coco as a potential 2027 long idea, pointing to improving sales momentum and opportunities for margin expansion if freight costs decline. BofA maintains a "buy" rating and a $72 price target.

Constellation Brands

BofA sees potential for an improving U.S. economic and immigration backdrop to support Constellation's business, given that around 40% of its consumers are Hispanic. The bank has a $160 price target, although its formal stock rating remains "neutral".
